research_question: In adults aged 18 years or older living with obesity, what is the effect of once-weekly tirzepatide at any dose, administered for at least 6 months, compared with placebo, on percentage change in body weight from baseline at medium-term follow-up (6 to 24 months)?
treatment_label: Once-weekly tirzepatide (any dose; dose arms combined where appropriate)
outcome_description: Percentage change in body weight from baseline, expressed in percentage points, at the assessment closest to the end of the 6-to-24-month window. Search for and extract this outcome whether primary or secondary and wherever reported in text, tables, figures, or legends. Prefer, in order: (1) adjusted tirzepatide-minus-placebo estimated treatment difference with 95% CI from ANCOVA or a mixed model under any estimand, used directly with SE=(upper CI-lower CI)/3.92; (2) arm-level estimated or least-squares means with SE or 95% CI, converting SE to SD as SE*sqrt(n); (3) arm-level raw means with SDs. Use analysed n when reported, otherwise randomised n; randomised n is appropriate for treatment-regimen analyses. For multi-dose trials, use a reported pooled tirzepatide group; otherwise combine dose arms by pooling means and SDs and summing n, or, if only dose-specific treatment differences are available, use 15 mg versus placebo. For randomised-withdrawal trials, measure change from randomisation through the randomised period; likewise use change from randomisation after an intensive lifestyle lead-in. Combine two sub-studies within one paper when arm-level data permit, or retain their separate tirzepatide-versus-placebo estimates within the trial when only separate contrasts are available. Exclude follow-up beyond 24 months and off-treatment periods. Do not extract or pool body weight in kg, BMI, waist circumference, categorical weight-loss thresholds, adverse events, cardiovascular events, quality of life, mortality, glycaemic outcomes, lipid outcomes, or any outcome other than percentage body weight change.
positive_direction: For standardized directional coding, a positive Hedges g would mean a greater reduction in percentage body weight with tirzepatide than with placebo (favouring tirzepatide). For the explicitly requested raw mean difference, retain the stated tirzepatide-minus-placebo scale, so MD below 0 percentage points means greater weight loss and favours tirzepatide.
search_queries: tirzepatide obesity placebo randomized trial body weight percentage change
tirzepatide once weekly placebo controlled weight loss adults
tirzepatide obesity comorbidity randomized placebo percentage body weight outcome
inclusion_criteria: Original parallel-group randomised controlled trials comparing once-weekly tirzepatide at any dose with placebo in adults aged 18 years or older living with obesity, including populations with comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes, prediabetes, obstructive sleep apnoea, or heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

Tirzepatide exposure and randomised comparison lasting at least 6 months, with an eligible on-treatment assessment between 6 and 24 months; randomised-withdrawal and intensive-lifestyle-lead-in designs are eligible when change is measured from randomisation.

Reports percentage change in body weight from baseline quantitatively as an adjusted treatment difference with uncertainty, arm-level estimated means with SE/CI, or arm-level raw means with SDs, including when this is a secondary outcome or appears only in results text, tables, figures, or figure legends.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study: exclude systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers.

No eligible treatment-control comparison: exclude studies without a tirzepatide-versus-placebo randomised comparison, nonrandomised studies, cross-over trials, active-comparator-only trials, and comparisons shorter than 6 months or assessed only outside the 6-to-24-month window.

No quantitative percentage-body-weight-change data capable of producing the requested effect size, such as an estimated difference with 95% CI, arm means with SD/SE/CI, t/F statistics, proportions, or other sufficient statistics; threshold p-values alone are insufficient when no usable estimate is reported.

Completely unrelated to tirzepatide treatment of adults living with obesity or reporting only ineligible outcomes such as weight in kg, BMI, waist circumference, categorical weight-loss response, safety, cardiovascular events, quality of life, mortality, glycaemic measures, or lipids.
moderators_to_extract: Tirzepatide dose strategy (pooled doses, fixed dose, maximum tolerated dose, or highest-dose contrast)
Participant comorbidity or clinical population (e.g., type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnoea, HFpEF, or obesity without the specified comorbidity)
Follow-up duration in weeks/months within the 6-to-24-month window
Trial design and baseline anchor (standard parallel group, randomised withdrawal, or lifestyle lead-in)
Estimand/analysis type and source of estimate (treatment-regimen vs efficacy; adjusted direct contrast vs arm-level data)
Background co-intervention or sub-study stratum (e.g., intensive lifestyle intervention or background therapy)
effect_size_note: Pool tirzepatide-minus-placebo mean differences in percentage points using a random-effects model. Preserve the raw sign convention: MD < 0 indicates more weight loss with tirzepatide and favours tirzepatide. For an adjusted treatment difference and 95% CI, use the contrast directly and calculate SE=(upper-lower)/3.92; do not require arm SDs, an exact p-value, or an F statistic. For arm-level estimates, derive SD from SE as SD=SE*sqrt(n) where needed. Use analysed n if stated, otherwise randomised n. Avoid double-counting a shared placebo: preferentially pool tirzepatide dose arms; if this is impossible because only dose-specific contrasts are reported, select 15 mg versus placebo. Assign arms from treatment descriptions rather than column order. Use one assessment per trial, closest to the end of the 6-to-24-month window, and exclude extensions after 24 months and off-treatment periods. Quantify heterogeneity (tau-squared and I-squared), report the pooled MD with 95% CI and prediction interval when estimable, examine influence/outliers and prespecified moderators when enough studies are available, and assess small-study effects only when the number of independent comparisons is adequate. Document study selection with a PRISMA 2020 flow diagram, duplicate screening/extraction, risk-of-bias assessment using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence using GRADE.
single_outcome_target: percentage change in body weight from baseline
